publicDiscovery.authentication: None; no Authorization, Cookie, URL credentials or applicant fields.
publicDiscovery.scope: Selected public Greenhouse and Lever boards across locations/professions; not a complete worldwide job index.

coverage: Blank general-audience Start/Profile flow preserves internal product/storage identity and prior user records.
Application profile and planning notes are clearly separate; new planning editors do not expose unused legacy SAR filters.
Incomplete add-link drafts survive dismissal/background/relaunch without a service call, preserve earlier saved draft on invalid edits, and consume only an exact matching successfully saved draft.
A discovered or legacy opportunity is explicitly copied to the existing application workspace; canonical identity avoids duplicate links and preserves separate original notes/status.
Public discovery requests use a fixed HTTPS origin and explicit fields only, with cookies/credentials disabled and redirects refused.
Unknown provider geography and work arrangement remain unknown; freshness and partial availability are retained.
Delayed/cancelled search responses cannot overwrite changed criteria or a later search; malformed responses and all-source outages preserve prior results.
Pagination deduplicates stable IDs, keeps the exact query/cursor, and stops on snapshot changes until an explicit new search.
Retry-After prevents early search repetition; saved board limits and corrupted-cache preservation are exercised.
Existing exact approval, receipt, uncertainty, cooldown, conflict, resume-byte and connection-generation protections continue through the production lifecycle suite.

limitations: No local Xcode project build, simulator launch, physical-device run, signing, installation or distribution was performed.

The first hosted iPhone Simulator attempt ran seven tests with five passes and two failures. Its exact evidence and targeted corrections are recorded separately; no runtime pass is claimed for the revised source until the next hosted run.
Standalone typechecking does not validate linked app/resource packaging, rendered UI, VoiceOver behavior, keyboard/PDF-picker presentation or device file protection.
The lifecycle/discovery executables use production stores with synthetic dependencies and real temporary files, not live browser sign-in, hosted pairing or employer APIs.
No real employer application was submitted; live verification still requires provider acceptance with an application ID.
The current public discovery service and production native pairing flow require their own deployed-service acceptance evidence.
Shared-Mac build-slot acknowledgment remains required before any local Xcode/simulator work; the separate hosted UI job does not grant that local slot.
